Launching a direct-to-consumer skincare brand

A sample project showing how we would take a new online brand from identity to first orders.

Project

Launching a direct-to-consumer skincare brand

Industry

E-commerce / Beauty

Challenge

A new skincare brand has a good product but no identity, no store and no audience. It needs to earn trust quickly in a crowded category, and cash-on-delivery habits mean the checkout and fulfilment experience matters as much as the advertising.

Strategy

Position the brand around a clear point of difference, build a fast mobile-first store with simple checkout options that suit local buying habits, and test Meta ad creative and audiences methodically. Measure from first click to confirmed order, including delivery outcomes.

Execution

  • Positioning workshop, messaging and visual identity
  • Mobile-first store with product pages built around customer questions
  • Cash-on-delivery and online payment options set up
  • Creative testing across short video, carousel and static ads
  • Order, return and delivery tracking in analytics
  • Email and WhatsApp follow-up flows with consent

Tools and platforms

  • Meta Ads Manager
  • Google Analytics 4
  • Google Tag Manager
  • A suitable e-commerce platform

Results

No results are claimed. This is a demonstration, so there is no real performance data. In a real case study this section reports verified figures supplied by the client. We would report measures such as:

  • Cost per confirmed order
  • Order confirmation and delivery rates
  • Return rates
  • Repeat purchase rate
  • Contribution of each channel to orders

Services involved

  • Branding
  • Website Design
  • Meta Ads
  • Analytics & CRO
